From e0d4675789499b5955aa05ef9abc2926b30ba4ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2014 11:29:09 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] kill: fix bug in --all semantic

Introduces by 2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41.

Signed-off-by: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>

diff --git a/misc-utils/kill.c b/misc-utils/kill.c
index 37f4c6e34..d461b36a6 100644
--- a/misc-utils/kill.c
+++ b/misc-utils/kill.c
@@ -486,7 +486,7 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv)
 
 			if (!ps)
 				continue;
-			if (ctl.check_all)
+			if (!ctl.check_all)
 				proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
 
 			proc_processes_filter_by_name(ps, ctl.arg);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `misc-utils/kill.c`**
   - The condition checking for `ctl.check_all` was modified from `if (ctl.check_all)` to `if (!ctl.check_all)`. This change alters the logic to filter processes by user ID only when `check_all` is false, instead of when it is true.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `kill.c` directly addresses a bug related to the `--all` option's semantics. By changing the condition to check for the negation of `ctl.check_all`, the patch ensures that the filtering by user ID occurs only when the `--all` option is not specified. This change corrects the behavior introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41`), which likely caused unintended process filtering when the `--all` option was used.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (ctl.check_all)
    proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
```
Reason:
The logical condition incorrectly checks if `ctl.check_all` is true, which leads to filtering processes by user ID when the `--all` option is specified. This is contrary to the expected behavior, where all processes should be included without filtering.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!ctl.check_all)
    proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
```
Reason:
By changing the condition to check if `ctl.check_all` is false, the filtering by user ID is only applied when the `--all` option is not specified. This ensures that all processes are included when the `--all` option is used, thus fixing the bug.
